notModeled.title: Interactions not modeled
notModeled.description: The current model includes main effects only. A zero here means the interaction term was not estimated, not that the process has no interaction. Use DOE Quadratic or an interaction model to test it.

explicit.title: Explicit interactions modeled

implicit.title: Interactions captured implicitly

hybrid.title: Interactions depend on the hybrid model

modelCenter.shapAdvice: Mean impact magnitude is shown; signs indicate output direction and do not prove causality.

timeSeries.title: Time-Series Foundation
timeSeries.foundationNotice: This Phase 1 workflow filters the trailing day window, prepares historical features, and creates chronological validation evidence. Forecast-performance metrics require a fitted time-series estimator in a later phase.

explanation.title: Time-Series Model Explanation
explanation.nonCausalTitle: Model evidence is not causal evidence
explanation.nonCausalDescription: Feature importance, block-permutation sensitivity, and conditional interactions describe predictive associations within this model and data range only. Confirm causal effects with a targeted DOE or engineering experiment.
explanation.sensitivityDescription: A larger MAE increase means predictions rely more on that feature after chronological blocks are reordered. This is model sensitivity, not causal effect size.
explanation.interactionsDescription: Strength measures how a feature's model contrast changes across quantile strata of the conditioning feature. These pairs are model-inferred hypotheses for experimental confirmation.

desc.doeLinear:
Linear model with main effects only. Target: continuous. Requires ≥3 inputs.

Applicable scenarios: Quick baseline model; screening experiments with few factors; when interpretability matters more than accuracy; DOE Phase 1 analysis.
desc.doeQuadratic:
Linear + interaction + squared terms. Target: continuous. Requires ≥2 inputs.

Applicable scenarios: Response surface optimization; capturing curvature in factor effects; when interactions between inputs are expected; DOE Phase 2 analysis.
desc.randomForest:
Ensemble of decision trees (regression). Target: continuous. Handles non-linear relationships.

Applicable scenarios: Complex non-linear processes; many input features; when feature importance ranking is needed; robust to outliers and noise; no distribution assumptions required.
desc.residualHybrid:
DOE linear + Random Forest on residuals. Target: continuous. Combines interpretability & accuracy.

Applicable scenarios: Processes with both linear trends and complex non-linear residuals; when you need both interpretability (DOE part) and accuracy (RF residual part); best of both worlds.
desc.logisticRegression:
Binary classification model. Target: binary (0/1 or two categories only). Predicts probability of class.

Applicable scenarios: Pass/fail prediction; NG/OK classification; quality control decision making; when you need probability scores not just yes/no; interpreting feature impact on defect probability.
desc.weibullRegression:
Reliability / time-to-failure model. Target: strictly positive continuous. Estimates shape k & scale λ.

Applicable scenarios: Product lifetime analysis; wear-out / failure time prediction; reliability engineering; when output represents time, duration, or lifespan; maintenance scheduling optimization.
desc.xgboost:
Gradient boosting trees (regression). Target: continuous. Fast & accurate; supports auto feature selection.

Applicable scenarios: High-dimensional data with many features; when prediction accuracy is the top priority; feature selection built-in; faster training than random forest; industrial process optimization.
desc.lightgbm:
Gradient boosting trees (regression). Target: continuous. High performance with leaf-wise growth; supports auto feature selection.

Applicable scenarios: Large datasets (100k+ rows); when training speed matters; leaf-wise tree growth captures complex patterns; preferred over XGBoost for very large data. Note: GPU training requires NVIDIA CUDA + recompilation; Apple MPS is not supported.

copula.title: Joint Anomaly Probability
copula.noAnomalies: Need at least 2 anomalies for Copula analysis.
copula.description: Compute joint occurrence probabilities for multiple anomaly scenarios, using an independent assumption, a Gaussian Copula with a correlation matrix, or direct pair-wise joint probabilities.
copula.noAnomalySource: No anomaly scenarios are available. Run anomaly detection (Data Import / Exploration) first.
copula.summary: This analysis used {{mode}} for {{count}} anomaly scenarios. Compare each joint probability with the independent expectation: a higher value indicates increased co-occurrence risk, while a lower value indicates less co-occurrence. If a high-probability combination can increase NG, include it in Monte Carlo scenarios and investigate common causes by batch, machine, operator, and time. Results depend on sample size, anomaly definitions, and the correlation matrix; correlation is not causation.

grr.summaryAdvice: %GRR={{pct}}%, part-to-part={{part}}%; repeatability SD={{repeatability}}, reproducibility SD={{reproducibility}}. Use the verdict and application requirements together; for marginal or unacceptable results, check fixture stability and calibration first, then operator consistency and remeasure. GRR depends on part range and study design.

distribution.title: Distribution fitting
distribution.purpose: Compare candidate distributions for the selected column.
distribution.principle: AIC/BIC compare relative fit; the KS test checks consistency with a candidate.
distribution.interpretation: Lower AIC/BIC is preferable among candidates; a larger KS p-value means the distribution is not rejected by this sample.
distribution.limits: A sample fit does not prove the population follows the distribution.
distribution.recommendation: Use the selected distribution as a simulation starting point only after checking parameters, plots, and engineering plausibility.
